The app is built and works end to end. `npx @angular/cli@19 serve` starts it, and signing in with `admin` / `admin` reaches the dashboard. The production build has no warnings.

## What I checked in a real browser (Playwright, 1280px and 375px wide)
- **Routing and guards:** `/` goes to `/login`. Opening `/login` while signed in goes to `/dashboard`. `/users` while signed out goes back to `/login`. Signing in sets `isLoggedIn: true` in localStorage; signing out removes it.
- **Login form:** submitting it empty puts both fields into an error state with a message.
- **Dashboard:** a new log line appears every 3 seconds.
- **Profile menu:** it opens leftward and stays fully on screen at both widths (right edge at 1216 of 1280, and 351 of 375). It closes on an outside click or Escape.
- **Create, read, update, delete:** all four go through the in-memory API and the table reflects each one:
  - **Edit:** changing "John" to "Johnny" updates the row.
  - **Delete:** "Delete user" in the edit dialog opens the confirmation with the right member and removes the row.
  - **Invite:** adds a member as Active with today's date.
  - **Details:** shows "Member since January 2024" with all four fields disabled.
- **Dialogs:** all four open and close (Close button, X, Escape, backdrop click).
- **Console:** no errors or warnings.

## The token resolver
I asked it before writing any CSS, and the answers changed the code:
- **Chart bars (pure black):** it refused. Your spec asks for "the darkest foreground colour available", so I used the darkest filled surface the tokens do have (#111), and left a comment on that rule saying black has no token.
- **Shadows on cards:** for a login card and dashboard tiles it only offered the modal shadow, with low confidence, and the nearest real match is the dropdown shadow. The guide says not to pick the nearest, so cards have a border and no shadow. Figma shows a soft shadow, so this is a visible difference.
- **Ambiguous answers:** for link colour and menu-item hover it couldn't decide between two tokens. I chose the primary text colour (the spec asks for it) and the tertiary-button hover colour.
- **Two answers I overrode:** for the large metric value and the login heading it suggested the 15px size. Figma shows 26px and 22px, so I used the 22px token described as "largest display text".
- **Disabled fields:** asked directly, it refused. Asking how the input component styles itself led me to the component's own `disabled` state, so the details dialog uses real disabled inputs instead of hand-made boxes.

No hex values, pixel values, tier 1 tokens or tier 3 tokens appear in the app's code. A scan confirms it.

## Literals I wrote, because no token exists
- **Fonts:** the token set has no font-family values. `styles.css` defines a sans stack (Inter first) and a monospace stack for the logs.
- **Breakpoints:** the dashboard grid uses 640px and 1024px. There are no breakpoint tokens, and CSS variables can't be used in media queries anyway.

## Where I followed the spec over Figma
- **Text:** Figma's copy differs in many places ("Sign in to your account", "2,847", a "System Status" tile, a "Queue Worker" row). I used the spec's text and tile list everywhere.
- **Dashboard layout:** there are 8 tiles on a 12-column grid. The four metrics are in one row, then Throughput beside Service Health, then Data Summary beside System Logs. Figma has no separate Data Summary tile, so I placed that row myself.
- **Logs:** they follow Figma's light card style, in a monospace font, rather than a dark terminal look.
- **Table:** it has separate Avatar and Name columns as the spec says; Figma combines them.
- **Row buttons:** Details is the least emphasised, Edit secondary and Delete red, per the spec. Figma gives the least emphasis to Edit.
- **Header and footer:** the library header has no slot for the profile control, so I placed it over the header's right edge. Links in the header and footer go through the Angular router, so navigation doesn't reload the page. The footer has brand, link columns and legal links as the spec asks, which is more than Figma's single line.
- **Dialogs:** the library modal has no dividers above and below the body, and its padding is 20px where Figma shows 24px. I didn't override the component's internals.

## Setup notes
- `node_modules` came with Angular 21 packages installed, which conflicted with Angular 19. I deleted them and reinstalled cleanly.
- Port 4311 was taken by a process that wasn't mine, so I tested on port 4744.
